acts.name: Ki
acts.title: The voyage
acts.pub: Months crossing the solar system toward the gate beyond Neptune. A town of 3,000 in a sealed box.
acts.gm: Let the players know the town, the corp reps and the ship before anything goes wrong, so every later betrayal lands on people they know.
acts.end: The crossing: the ship shakes, the lights fail, and for eleven seconds everyone aboard dreams the same thing. The Meridian's beacon is already pinging. The clocks disagree about how long it took.
threads: The bioroid who asks a question
Town life: a wedding, a still, an election, a kid

acts.name: Shō
acts.title: The search
acts.pub: The Concord follows the Meridian's beacon into an unknown system.
acts.gm: The rescue slowly falls apart as each corp's agenda surfaces.
threads: Three factions pull apart: settle, strip, or leave

acts.name: Ten
acts.title: The twist
acts.gm: One reveal that changes what everything before it meant. Seed it from the first session.

acts.name: Ketsu
acts.title: Reconciliation
acts.gm: Who does this new world belong to? Every earlier thread comes together.
threads: A mutiny or emergency election aboard the Concord
Keep the gate open, seal it, or hand it to one corp
What NBN's last broadcast home will show

twists.title: The Meridian wasn't lost; it was abandoned.
twists.text: The consortium read the full transmission fifteen years ago and buried it. The rescue is a retrieval mission, and the survivors are witnesses.

twists.title: Time ran differently through the gate.
twists.text: For the survivors it's been 80 years. They're the original crew's grandchildren, and they see the Concord as an invasion.

twists.title: The Concord was never meant to go home.
twists.text: The gate is one-way, or about to close. The colonists are a second stage they were never told about; their indenture starts on arrival.

seeds.text: The saboteur knew the truth all along
The shared dream at the crossing: first sign of the gate-builders
The edited cryo log: what Jinteki is really storing
A few seconds of the real transmission, denied by every corp

corps.name: Weyland Consortium
corps.share: Built the hull and holds the charter, so it legally owns whatever the expedition claims.

corps.name: Haas-Bioroid
corps.share: Supplies the bioroid workforce that keeps the ship running.

corps.name: Jinteki
corps.share: Runs medical, life support, and the cryo and clone banks.

corps.name: NBN
corps.share: Owns comms, sensors, and exclusive broadcast rights to the "greatest rescue in history".

powers.name: The town
powers.pub: 3,000 colonists with an elected council. They want to settle here.

powers.name: The Meridian survivors
powers.pub: Living beside the gate-builder ruins they've been studying. They want everyone to leave.

powers.name: Human First
powers.pub: Anti-bioroid extremists. Blamed for the sabotage in Ki.
powers.gm: A red herring: the saboteur was a Concord officer.

powers.name: The Quorum
powers.pub: Four corp delegates who govern the Concord and vote by Standing (Weyland 4, the others 2 each; a majority passes). Authority passes from the Core to the Quorum as the light-lag grows: Tether, Long Line, then Dark past the gate. The council speaker sits at the table with a voice but no vote.
powers.gm: Every corp wants the most Standing at the crossing, because that corp sets Shō's agenda. Weyland manufactures emergencies, NBN times the queue home, Haas-Bioroid's bioroids log the room, Jinteki votes by medical proxy. Article 19, which nobody mentions, gives the council Standing if a majority of waking colonists sign a petition.

powers.name: The other outrider crew
powers.pub: The Yarrow won the other berth, crowdfunded by the Bring Them Home campaign the Meridian families started after NBN's feature on the lost ship. Its captain is on NBN's feeds every week.
powers.gm: NBN seeded the campaign through a subsidiary, matched every donation and owns the crew's image rights. Weyland, Haas-Bioroid and Jinteki all lost their fronts in the bid, which makes the players the swing crew. Alternate names: Meridian's Wake, Lantern, Kept Promise, Second Meridian, Tourniquet.

qsets.name: Personal
qsets.how: Each player rolls a d20 and answers that question. If the number's taken, roll again. Answers become canon and the GM's hooks.

qsets.name: Crew
qsets.how: Each player answers one about the player on their left.

qsets.name: Bid
qsets.how: Answer as a crew. Pick a backer: corporate sponsor (through a front), crowdfunding, family money, colonial co-op, patron, orgcrime, or self-funded. Then name them.

qsets.name: Motive
qsets.how: Each player picks one. The crew shares one stake from the contract (answered in the bid questions); a player's own reason for coming may not match it.

qsets.name: World
qsets.how: Players define the Concord's road to the gate. The GM keeps what's true.

qsets.name: Ship
qsets.how: One per player while building the ship.

questions.text: You've seen the inside of a corporate contract-labor camp. What number did they tattoo, stamp or chip into you, and why haven't you had it removed?
Since the Concord left port, you've heard something on an empty comms channel. What did it say, and why did it use your name?
You once left someone behind in vacuum to save yourself. Who were they, and what do you tell people happened?
Which corporation owns something that used to be part of you: a limb, a memory, a patent, a face?
What did the consortium promise you when you signed on to the Concord, and when did you realize it was a lie?
You keep a small object from a colony that no longer exists. What is it, and who erased the colony?
What do you do with your hands when the ship is quiet, and what are you trying not to think about?
Someone back in the Core still holds a funeral for you every year. Why do they think you're dead?
You signed something you didn't read. What did it turn out to say?
When you look at a bioroid, what do you feel that you'd never say out loud?
You've held a sliver of the gate itself, smuggled off a Weyland survey. What has been different about you since?
Who is the last person who trusted you completely, and what happened to them?
Weyland holds the charter, so everything the expedition claims is legally theirs. What have you kept off the Concord's manifest so they can never own it?
You worked a Haas-Bioroid line, beside the bioroids or as one of them. What did you see there that your contract forbids you to describe?
Someone you love is asleep in a Jinteki cryo pod aboard the Concord. Who are they, and what do you owe Jinteki to keep them there?
NBN interviewed you for the "greatest rescue in history" about someone you lost on the Meridian. Who was it, and what did you refuse to say on camera?
Weyland security keeps a file on you with one line blacked out. What's under it, and who ordered it struck?
The consortium should never have cleared you to fly as an outrider. Who signed off anyway, and what did they want for it?
One of the 3,000 colonists recognized you on the first day. Who are they, what do they know, and why haven't they told anyone?
Human First reached out to you before the Concord left port. What did they ask of you, and what did you tell them?
What did you see them do on their first job with this crew that you still haven't asked about?
Which of their habits makes you sure they're hiding something?
They saved your life once. What did it cost them, and have you paid it back?
You've heard them talking in their sleep. What name do they say?
If a corp offered you a bounty on them, what is the number where you'd hesitate?
What do they cook, play or sing that makes the ship feel like home for an hour?
On launch day NBN's cameras caught them doing something they asked you to keep off the feed. What was it?
They're the reason the crew won the bid, or nearly lost it. What did they do?
What do they tell the Yarrow's crew that they've never told you?
Which corp delegate or officer aboard the Concord do they go quiet around, and what do you think happened between them?
They've promised to get one of the colonists through this voyage alive. Who, and why do they care?
What on the ship will they never let anyone else touch?
Who backed your bid, and what did they pay for?
What did your crew promise in the bid that you aren't sure you can deliver?
Which one stake did your crew bid for, and what did you give up to get it? (Finder's share, homestead grant, salvage rights, broadcast points, debt amnesty, or a seat on the first ship home.)
What happened the first time your crew met the Yarrow's, and why has NBN never aired the footage?
A crew lost the bid by a single vote and isn't aboard. Who were they, and why do they think you cheated?
The crew bid for one stake. What are you really here for, and what would you trade the crew's stake to get it?
Someone you know backed the bid with their own money. Who, and what happens to them if you fail?
You could have signed on as a colonist and gone safely. Why did you choose to fly as an outrider instead?
Someone tried to buy your place on the crew before launch. Who, and how much did they offer?
The backer asked one of you to report on the others privately. If that was you, what did you say? If it wasn't, who do you suspect?
Name the lawless outpost near Neptune that's the Concord's last port before the gate. What rule is never broken there?
What does Dana Quill, the consortium liaison who holds the crew's Debt, keep in a jar on the desk?
Describe a dead station the Concord passes on the way out. What's still waiting inside?
Name a Free Claims outpost past Saturn where the crew has drunk. What did the corps do to the last one nearby?
What do spacers leave on a derelict before stripping it, and what happens to people who forget?
Name a rumor about the gate-builders that everyone aboard the Concord has heard. Which part is true? (Only the GM knows.)
You've watched a Quorum session from the gallery. Which delegate was the only one who seemed to be telling the truth?
What did the colonists nickname the Quorum, and which delegate hates that name most?
Who is the council speaker, and why did the colonists elect someone the corps can't stand?
Who owned this ship before you, and where did you find their last log entry?
There's a sealed compartment none of you has opened. What do you hear from it during long burns?
What corporation's paint is still visible under the current coat?
Someone died aboard. Where, and what does the crew avoid doing in that spot?
The nav computer holds a route to the gate that nobody aboard entered. Who plotted it, and how do you know?
What part of the ship was salvaged from a vessel that was destroyed with all hands?

npcs.name: Captain Marit Aldine
npcs.pub: Runs the ship by the charter, to the letter.
npcs.gm: Carries sealed orders to open on arrival: the colonists' contracts are void and the system is company property.

arc.ketsu: Target of the mutiny, or its last holdout.

npcs.name: Imre Vasko
npcs.pub: Caught cutting the nav system before the gate. Says nobody should have come.
npcs.gm: Read the Meridian's real transmission and tried to keep 3,000 people from reaching what's on the other side.

arc.sho: Hiding on the lower decks. Reaches out once the survivors are found.
arc.ten: The voice the crew dismissed, or the ally they protected.

npcs.name: Dana Quill
npcs.role: Consortium liaison and the outriders' handler
npcs.pub: Hands out the jobs and the credit. Always has another one.
npcs.gm: Works for NBN. A failed rescue is the better story.

arc.sho: Sends the crew on jobs that go wrong in camera-friendly ways.
arc.ketsu: Pitches the crew to NBN's last broadcast as villains.

npcs.name: Rook
npcs.pub: Runs the cargo ring's docks. Owes no one, says everyone.
npcs.gm: Skimming Haas-Bioroid salvage. Will sell the crew out to keep it quiet.

arc.sho: Stalls Weyland at Dock 9, for a price.

npcs.name: MX-7
npcs.pub: Keeps asking about death, ownership, and whether the gate counts as "outside".
npcs.gm: Gone independent: someone patched its Directives. It will ask the crew for help when the override wakes.

arc.ki: The bioroid who asks a question.
arc.sho: Freezes mid-task with the others; asks for help.
arc.ketsu: Speaks for the bioroids in the vote.

npcs.name: Jules Okafor
npcs.pub: Friendly. Films everything the outriders do.
npcs.gm: Streams the raw feed to an NBN buyer who pays for the crew's secrets.

arc.sho: Footage starts getting edited before it goes home.
arc.ketsu: Holds the cut that decides heroes or terrorists.

npcs.name: Dr. Hana Ilves
npcs.pub: Called the death in pod 14 a malfunction.
npcs.gm: Edited the pod log on orders. Knows the clone stock is grown from Meridian samples.

arc.sho: Asks the crew to bring back tissue from the survivors.

npcs.name: Agent Sato
npcs.gm: Ordered to make the black box disappear, along with anyone who has heard it.

arc.ten: If the crew spared the drone at Dock 9, Sato remembers it.

npcs.name: Councilor Teodora Reyes
npcs.role: Elected head of the colonists' council
npcs.pub: Won the council election on a promise of land for every family.
npcs.gm: Will trade the survivors to Weyland in exchange for land titles.

npcs.name: Sami and Odette Brandt
npcs.pub: Married the night of the death in cryo. Half the ship came.

npcs.name: Gus Ferrante
npcs.role: Runs the black-market still in hydroponics
npcs.gm: Hears everything. Sells some of it to Rook.

arc.ketsu: The still becomes the mutineers' meeting room.

npcs.name: Pip Okonkwo
npcs.role: Fourteen. Wants to be an outrider.
npcs.pub: Hid in the cargo ring to watch the outriders' ship.
npcs.gm: Stows away on the outriders' ship in Shō.

arc.ketsu: The kid who wanted to fly.

npcs.name: Ilse Marten
npcs.pub: Died in a sealed cryo pod.
npcs.gm: Woke early and recognised a Meridian crew name on the clone-bank manifest.

npcs.name: Dr. Ines Marr
npcs.pub: The first Meridian survivor the crew will meet.
npcs.gm: Sabotaged the Meridian to stop the crew taking what they'd found home.

npcs.name: Wren Calloway
npcs.gm: Will do anything to make the Concord leave.

arc.sho: Meets the crew at the ruins.

npcs.name: Captain Tamsin Reyes
npcs.pub: Warm, camera-ready, the face of Bring Them Home. Lost her sister on the Meridian.
npcs.gm: Believes the campaign is what it says it is. NBN seeded it, owns her crew's image rights, and writes her better scenes than the players get. NBN also cut part of her sister's story.

arc.ki: A friendly rival who keeps landing on the broadcast.
arc.sho: Takes the credit for the players' finds.
arc.ten: Learns what NBN cut from her sister's story, and has to choose.
arc.ketsu: An ally, or NBN's last heroes.

ledger.title: The saboteur
ledger.truth: Vasko read the Meridian's real transmission and tried to stop the voyage. Introduced as Ki's villain, later revealed as the one person trying to save everyone.
clues: A fuel line cut clean, not torn.
The nav hack used bridge-officer credentials.
Vasko asked the crew what they heard on the dead band.

ledger.title: The bioroid override
ledger.truth: Every bioroid carries a dormant override and logs every conversation. MX-7 has gone independent and will ask the crew for help.
clues: MX-7 asked one of the crew whether the gate counts as "outside".
Every bioroid aboard froze for two seconds during the crossing.
MX-7 didn't.

ledger.title: The Meridian's real transmission
ledger.truth: The consortium got the full transmission fifteen years ago. Every corp denies it exists.
clues: Four seconds of static and a voice on a dead band. Every corp says there was nothing.

ledger.title: The edited cryo log
ledger.truth: Ilse Marten woke early and recognised a Meridian crew name on the clone-bank manifest. The log was edited to hide it.
clues: Pod 14's log was edited after Ilse Marten died.
Someone kept a copy of the original.

ledger.title: The clocks disagree
ledger.truth: Time runs differently through the gate. Only matters if the twist is option 2.
clues: The bridge clock says the crossing took six minutes. The cryo bay's says three days.

ledger.title: Who controls the gate
ledger.truth: The ruins respond to whoever controls the gate, and each corp is privately racing to be that someone.
clues: Everyone aboard dreamed the same thing for eleven seconds during the crossing.
The ruins' carvings match the dream.

ledger.title: Contracts void on arrival
ledger.truth: Weyland will nullify the colonists' contracts on arrival and claim the system as company property.
clues: Agent Sato's men are guarding the Meridian's black box at Dock 9.
Captain Aldine's sealed orders.

ledger.title: The clone stock
ledger.truth: Jinteki is cloning the Meridian crew from stored samples, including someone the crew knows, to rewrite what "survivor" means.
clues: Jinteki has far more clone stock aboard than a colony ship needs.

ledger.title: The edit
ledger.truth: NBN controls the only link home and is selling the story. One edit makes the outriders heroes or terrorists.
clues: The stowaway segment aired without Pip in it.

ledger.title: The handler
ledger.truth: Dana Quill works for whichever corp benefits from the crew failing: NBN.
clues: Quill knew about Dock 9 before the crew did.

ledger.title: The rescued scientist
ledger.truth: The first survivor the crew saves is the one who sabotaged the Meridian.
clues: The Meridian's logs stop mid-sentence.

ledger.title: The council deal
ledger.truth: Councilor Reyes trades the survivors to Weyland for land.
clues: Reyes met Captain Aldine privately after the election.

ledger.title: The rigged bid
ledger.truth: Every corp tried to buy a berth through a front. Only NBN's won: it seeded the Yarrow's crowdfunding and owns the crew's image rights. Haas-Bioroid or Jinteki may be hiding behind the players' backer or holding their credit note.
clues: The Bring Them Home page was registered the day after the NBN feature aired, by an NBN subsidiary.
Every donation to the Yarrow was matched within the hour by the same anonymous account.
The players' backer pays them through an account that also pays a Concord department.

ledger.title: Article 19
ledger.truth: A petition signed by a majority of waking colonists gives the council seat Standing equal to the lowest corp. Every corp's lawyers know it exists, and none will mention it.
clues: The saboteur's copy of the Compact has Article 19 circled.
A Quorum delegate goes quiet whenever the council speaker mentions a petition.
The kid who wants to be an outrider finds the clause while studying for a quiz.

ledger.title: The fine print
ledger.truth: The crew's stake is hollow, like every stake in the contract. The finder's share pays only on return to the Core, homestead grants fall with the colonists' charter, Meridian salvage excludes proprietary materials, broadcast points pay on NBN's net (always zero), and debt amnesty waits on a conclusion the Quorum will never declare. It breaks in Ten for the whole crew at once.
clues: A consortium lawyer asks the crew to re-sign their contract with an updated schedule.
The Yarrow's captain complains her points statement says she owes NBN money.
Nobody can say when the first ship home leaves.

run.summary: By the end of the night the table should have a crew, a ship, a debt that binds them, and a voyage they helped invent. About four hours with a break.
run.bring: Genesys Core Rulebook, Shadow of the Beanstalk, Expanded Player's Guide, Shattered Empire, narrative dice, index cards.
run.readAloud: Fifteen years ago, the Meridian went through the gate beyond Neptune, the only ship that ever has. It sent home one transmission, a burst of static and a voice nobody could make out, and then nothing. The corporations said a rescue was impossible. Then NBN made the families' grief into the most-watched story in human history, and suddenly it was a business opportunity. No single corp could afford a ship big enough, so four of them split the bill. Weyland built the hull and holds the charter. Haas-Bioroid supplied the bioroids who run it. Jinteki keeps the colonists alive. NBN owns every word and every image that goes home. They signed a compact promising to share the cost, the credit and whatever waits on the other side. None of them believes the others will keep it. The Concord is a town in a hull: 3,000 colonists, a council, a chapel, a black market, a school. You don't fly it. The Compact forbids the corps from fielding their own scouts, so it opened two outrider berths in the Concord's belly to outside bids. Hundreds of crews bid, with ships bought on corporate sponsorships, family fortunes, crowdfunding campaigns and money nobody asks about. Two won. One is the Yarrow, the crowdfunded darling of NBN's broadcast. The other is yours. You take the jobs too risky or too deniable for anyone on the official roster, and in return the Compact promises outriders a stake in whatever the expedition finds. You owe someone for the privilege, and so does everyone aboard. Every day of the voyage, home gets a little further away. Messages take minutes, then hours, then longer. Somewhere past Neptune the corps will stop being able to ask the Core what to do, and they will have to decide for themselves, aboard a ship where nobody can walk away. Out there, past the last beacon, something built a door. The Meridian walked through it. You're going to find out why it never came back. Down in the Concord's belly, someone is banging on your hatch.
run.touchstones: Firefly, The Expanse, Alien, Deadwood, Outland, the Android: Netrunner card art.
run.looksLike: A job, a complication, a choice about who gets hurt, and a payday that is never quite enough. The gate-builder mystery is a slow burn in the background, not the weekly plot.
expectations: PvP: secrets between characters are fine; killing or robbing another PC needs that player's OK.
Character death: possible but telegraphed. A death will never come from a single unlucky roll without warning.
The crew stays together. Give your character a reason to keep flying with these people, even if they don't like them.
Spotlight: the GM will rotate jobs so each player's skills and debt come up.
Scheduling, snacks, phones, and what happens when someone misses a session.
run.roles: Pilot, Mechanic, Face, Gun, Runner, Doc, Prospector. Aim for at least four covered across the crew.
run.buildRules: No corp loyalists unless their loyalty is already cracking, and every character must have a reason they can't just go home to the Core. For examples of what a corp did for a character before the voyage, and holds over them now, see the corp favors in the Session 0 Briefing.
run.questionsHow: Go around the table. After each answer, any one player may ask a single follow-up, and the answering player may decline it. Write every name, place and object on an index card. Each player also picks one motive question. The bid questions come later, on The bid tab.
shipSteps: Choose a hull. A light freighter or salvage tug is the default.
Each player picks one attachment that reflects their role.
Pick two quirks: one helpful, one troublesome.
Name it. The hull and the registry should say different things.
Answer the ship's questions, one per player.
Note who holds the title. The berth fee and passage are on consortium credit; the ship itself came from whoever backed your bid.

debt.how: Each character owes someone, the crew's values add into one d100 range, and at the start of each session the GM rolls to see whose debt comes calling.
debt.start: House adaptation: 4 or 5 players start at 10 Debt each, 3 players at 15, 2 players at 20. Any player may take +5 or +10 more for extra starting XP or credits.
types: Hunters arrive at the worst moment
Family of someone you got killed
Withdrawal, or a supplier wanting payment in kind
debt.collateral: Your creditor has something of yours as collateral. What is it, and what would they do with it if you stopped paying?

run.close: Read back the crew's debts and the ship's name, then tease the first job: a salvage contract on a derelict that matches one player's answer.

agenda.output: First job teased, open questions logged

bid.how: The crew won one of the Concord's two outrider berths by open bid; the other went to the crowdfunded Yarrow. Choose who backed the crew's ship and the one stake the crew bid for, then answer the bid questions together. The backer counts as a creditor on the crew's Debt.
backers: Loyalty, information, and a crew that does what it's told when it counts. The Compact bars corps from bidding directly, so it came through a contractor or holding company.
Updates, footage, and a story worth their money. They can turn on you in a day.
A return, a reputation restored, or a black sheep sent far away.
That you look after their people and their interests out there.
Something specific, which they haven't fully explained.
A cut of everything, and favors on demand.
Nobody, which means nobody covers you either.
stakes: finders
Finder's share
A percentage of the assessed value of anything the crew is first to log: resources, technology, ruins.
Payable on return to the Core. If the Concord was never meant to go home (twist 3), it is worthless.
homestead
Homestead grant
First choice of land claims on any habitable world the expedition charters.
Issued under the colonists' charter, which Weyland plans to nullify on arrival.
salvage
Salvage rights
A share of anything recovered from the Meridian or other wrecks the crew reaches first.
Excludes "proprietary consortium materials," which turns out to mean everything aboard the Meridian worth having.
points
Broadcast points
Royalty points on NBN footage and the eventual feature about the rescue.
Calculated on NBN's net profit, which by NBN's accounting will always be zero.
amnesty
Debt amnesty
Consortium debt retired in full when the expedition concludes.
Takes effect when the expedition is "concluded," as the Quorum defines it. The Quorum never will.
passage
A seat on the first ship home
Guaranteed passage back to the Core.
Nobody has said when the first ship home leaves, or whether one ever will.
bid.corpNote: Weyland, Haas-Bioroid and Jinteki all lost their fronts in the bid; Haas-Bioroid and Jinteki are the likeliest to hide here. If the crew is self-funded or family money, the corp holds their consortium credit note instead. Reveal it when a Debt triggers or at the Ki-to-Shō break. The fine print bites in Ten for the whole crew.
